name: Coffee Pub Blacksmith
tagline: Toolbar, timers, combat stats and shared styling for Foundry.
description: The hub of the suite: a top-of-screen toolbar with dice tray, party health, notes and macros, synced combat and planning timers, combat statistics with leaderboards, a drag-and-drop initiative tracker and a live CSS editor. Every other Coffee Pub module builds on it.
pitch: A toolbar of dice, party health, timers and combat stats across the top of Foundry, plus the shared styling that powers every other Coffee Pub module.

features.title: Top toolbar
features.text: Dice tray, party health overview, status effects for the selected token, notes, and macros in one bar.

features.title: Synced timers
features.text: Combat and planning timers stay synced across clients, with pause, resume, and auto-start on move or attack.

features.title: Combat statistics
features.text: Hits, misses, damage, healing, kills, crits and an MVP per player and session, with leaderboards and history.

features.title: Combat tracker
features.text: Drag-and-drop initiative, health bars, and portraits.

features.title: Movement modes
features.text: Switch between normal, none, combat, follow, and conga line from the toolbar.

features.title: Themes and CSS editor
features.text: Styled chat and sidebar shared across Coffee Pub modules, plus a live CSS editor inside Foundry.

steps: Install socketlib and lib-wrapper from Foundry's module list.
Install Blacksmith with its manifest URL.
Enable all three in Manage Modules; settings live under Configure Settings, Coffee Pub Blacksmith.

points.x: The hub does the plumbing, and each module does its own experience. Windows, toolbars, sockets, toasts and compendium indexing are solved once.
Windows, toolbar and menubar tools, pin types, tags, importers and toast channels all plug in without special cases.
One hook layer with priorities, cleanup and error isolation, and one socket layer that works with or without SocketLib.
Every API page names its audience, pairs with an architecture page, and follows one written standard across the suite.
